edits.replace:
- **Just landed.** Part 6 of the re-review, which is the last part of issue #223 with anything owed in it, and both halves of it corrected a claim rather than adding a capability. The deferral with no owner is refused by name: neither a load nor a mount seeds a flush, and the mount half was drafted the other way, implemented, and refused by a `CI` run rather than by a reading. A seed there contradicts the asymmetry `T-1` owns, breaks the promise that a time Motion does not emit before its first tick, and, because `PatchRegistry.publish` drops a candidate through `samePatch`, takes the next publication instead of adding one, which is 18 of the 21 cases it turned red. The second half is what C3's declined build stopped owning: a fresh `Track` was the only thing that dropped a live value write, so the four binding verbs had begun keeping an override the file above says they drop, and the predicate now builds when a live write is in force while the resolve stays unconditional. `RA-100` through `RA-105` are its evidence and [ADR-066](./ADR-066-load-and-mount-publish-nothing.md) records both, with the refused prescription kept under alternatives because the `samePatch` interaction is invisible from the call site. Issue #176, which part 6 named as the one tracked item, was completed by [#178](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/pull/178) on 21 August.
- **Landed just before it.** The flush a removal owes the nodes that were reading it, which is the fourth finding
